newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks close firm, buoyed by property investors.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks close firm, buoyed by property investors.

text.p: Property investment counters lifted Hong Kong stocks to a higher close on Friday after a major commercial and office building sold for a rich price in the territory, but profit-taking in other areas limited gains.
The Hang Seng index rose 17.23 points to 13,116.79. Turnover was HK$10.46 billion compared to HK$10.68 billion on Thursday.
Over the week the index advanced 227.42 points, or 1.76 percent.
"I believe people are just starting to rerate the property investors because of the Entertainment Building deal," said Kelvin Tang, analyst at ImPac Asset Management (HK) Ltd.
Chinese Estates Holdings Ltd said on Friday it had agreed to sell its Entertainment Building in Hong Kong's Central district to Hysan Development Ltd for HK$3.64 billion.

"The selling price for the Entertainment Building is more than satisfactory," said Patrick Chia, research director at China Everbright Research. "If the general property market bounces back, then I think a lot of property counters' net asset value should be adjusted upwards."
Shares in Chinese Estates closed at HK$9.10, up HK$0.05, after hitting a session high of HK$9.35. Hysan Development fell HK$0.75 to HK$28.15.
The transaction buoyed shares in Swire Pacific, up HK$3.00 at HK$75.25. "Swire compared with other hongs or property companies has actually underperformed the market," said Chia.

Great Eagle Holdings was another beneficiary, rising HK$2.40 to HK$31.00. "If a portfolio has a large portion of office buildings and retail space, then the net asset value will be raised," said Tang.
Amoy Properties gained HK$0.55 to HK$11.10 and Wharf Holdings rose HK$1.00 to HK$37.70.
However, banking giant and index heavyweight HSBC Holdings fell HK$1.50 to HK$155.50.

"HSBC and Hang Seng are undergoing some correction but they have outperformed the market. I think it is profit-taking by some investors," said Tang. Analysts said there was also some concern about contracting margins on mortgages.
Bank of East Asia fell HK$0.20 to HK$33.40 but Hang Seng Bank recovered from an early fall to HK$90.00 to end the day HK$0.25 higher at HK$91.00.
Shell Electric dropped HK$0.60 to HK$5.45. The company said it planned to place 70 million new shares at HK$5.50 each to raise net proceeds of about HK$374 million.
